Why does my time.Ticker drift when the handler is slow?

Ask Question
Asked 6 days ago
Viewed 1k times

I have a loop that reads from a time.Ticker every second and writes a metrics snapshot to disk. Most of the time it works, but when the disk is slow, the snapshots stop lining up with whole seconds, and after an hour they are several seconds behind the wall clock.

t := time.NewTicker(time.Second)
for range t.C {
    writeSnapshot() // sometimes takes 1.5s
}

I expected the ticker to keep firing on the second, even if one write is slow. Is the ticker drifting, or am I misunderstanding how it works?

  • go
  • timer
kestrel
1,204

2 Answers

The ticker isn’t drifting. Its channel has a buffer of one, so when your handler is slower than the period, ticks are dropped, not queued. Each time you come back to the channel, you get whatever tick is waiting, which may be stale.

The drift you see comes from mixing the tick time with time.Now() in writeSnapshot. Use the value received from the channel instead:

for tick := range t.C {
    writeSnapshot(tick.Truncate(time.Second))
}

If a write can take longer than a second, move it to a separate goroutine with a bounded queue, so that a slow disk can never block the ticker loop.

Also worth knowing:

  • the ticker adjusts its interval to make up for slow receivers
  • Reset on a ticker is safe since Go 1.15

See the time.NewTicker documentation for the exact rules.

  • Thanks, truncating the tick fixed it. – kestrel
